title: Gemini Integration — Overview
description: Every metric the integration emits, organized by question.

panels.title: Health check
panels.description: Is it up, is it fast, is it failing, what is it costing

panels.title: Served RPS
panels.description: Successful inbound requests per second.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: Errors and unusable answers as a share of all inbound requests.

panels.title: Shed rate (503)
panels.description: Deliberate backpressure, not a fault. Non-zero means at capacity.

panels.title: In flight
panels.description: Inbound requests currently being served.

panels.title: Spent
panels.description: Actual spend from reported usage metadata.

panels.title: Budget left
panels.description: Thresholds are fractions of SERVICE_BUDGET_USD: red under 10%, orange under 25%, yellow under 50%.

panels.title: Recent runs — click one to window the dashboard to it
panels.description: Each entry is a k6 run recorded by scripts/k6run.py. Clicking re-windows every panel to that run. Runs also appear as shaded regions on the time series below, so a spike can be attributed to a specific configuration.

panels.title: Latency layers — where the time actually goes

options.content: `total = queue_wait + upstream + framework`. **upstream** is Vertex and is not ours to fix. **queue_wait** is our admission gate — growth here is the earliest saturation signal. **framework** is serialization, validation and event-loop scheduling. If the stack is dominated by upstream, our integration is not the problem.

panels.title: Latency composition, p99 (stacked)
panels.description: Four separate costs. Upstream sums every attempt, so a retried request does not charge its failed attempts to us. Retry backoff is deliberate waiting, not processing. Only the bottom two layers are code we can make faster. Quantiles are not strictly additive, so read proportions rather than exact sums.

panels.title: Our overhead vs vendor time
panels.description: Our overhead should stay flat as load rises. If it climbs with traffic, we are the bottleneck.

panels.title: Admission queue wait
panels.description: Rises before latency or errors do. The earliest saturation signal.

panels.title: Upstream calls by finish reason (stacked)
panels.description: MAX_TOKENS means truncated and unusable, billed in full. SAFETY is a content block. Only STOP is a complete answer.

panels.title: Retries by reason
panels.description: Retries are hand-rolled rather than delegated to the SDK precisely so they appear here instead of being invisible.

panels.title: Empty / unusable responses
panels.description: HTTP 200 with no usable text. Invisible to transport-level retry.

panels.title: Burn rate
panels.description: Dollars per hour at the current rate.

panels.title: Cost per usable answer
panels.description: Spend divided by answers we can actually use. The unit-economics number.

panels.title: Time to budget exhaustion
panels.description: Remaining budget at the current burn rate.

panels.title: Cumulative spend vs ceiling
panels.description: The ceiling series is derived as spent + remaining, so it tracks SERVICE_BUDGET_USD without the dashboard having to be told it. The dashed line is the build-time default.

panels.title: Token rate by kind (stacked)
panels.description: Thinking tokens bill at the output rate but produce no user-visible text.

panels.title: Thinking share of billed output
panels.description: Measured at 83.6% with dynamic thinking on a short-answer workload. High values mean paying output rates for reasoning nobody reads.

panels.title: Saturation and capacity — is the ceiling us or them?
Connection pool saturation
panels.description: In-flight divided by pool size. Sustained near 1.0 means the HTTP pool is the ceiling, not the vendor. Most commonly missed bottleneck in async LLM clients.

panels.title: Event loop lag
panels.description: Rising lag means the Python process is the constraint. When this climbs, vendor-side latency numbers from this process are not trustworthy.

panels.title: Retry budget remaining
panels.description: Token bucket capping retries as a share of traffic. Draining to zero means retries are being shed rather than amplifying load against an already-struggling backend.

panels.title: Load generator (k6) — is the rig itself the bottleneck?

options.content: `k6_dropped_iterations_total` **must stay at zero**. Anything above zero means k6 could not sustain the offered rate, so the run measured the generator rather than the service and every other number here is suspect. It is a k6 threshold, so such a run also exits non-zero.

panels.title: Dropped iterations (must be zero)
panels.description: Non-zero invalidates the run.

panels.title: k6 observed latency
panels.description: Client-observed, includes network transit the service cannot see.
